name_en: Hall's theorem for finite solvable groups

literal_source_claim_en: Existence of Hall subgroups in finite solvable groups.
candidate_claim_not_credited_as_statemen: For every finite solvable group G and selected set pi of primes, there exists a subgroup H whose order has prime support in pi and whose index has prime support disjoint from pi; the exact encoding and source scope are not yet frozen.
domain_and_universes: Candidate scope: G : Type u with Group G, Finite G, and IsSolvable G; a selected prime set pi; and H : Subgroup G. The pi representation, finite-carrier encoding, universe, explicit instances, and Hall predicate remain statement-phase decisions.
conclusion: Open as an exact expression: existence of a Hall pi-subgroup for every source-approved prime selection and finite solvable group.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake. The statement must settle empty pi, all primes, the trivial group, pi disjoint from the group-order support, and redundant primes not dividing the group order.
candidate_scope_not_credited: a predicate saying every prime divisor of Nat.card H lies in pi and every prime divisor of H.index lies outside pi
the equivalent factorization or largest pi-divisor cardinality formulation

an existence conclusion only, without adding the classical conjugacy or pi-subgroup-containment clauses
